summary: Copies a value — an ID, a key, a command — confirms in place with a check and "Copied" for two seconds, and announces it. When the clipboard refuses it says so, and hands over the text.
useWhen: a value is copied far more often than it is read — a run ID, an API key's prefix, a command, a link
the copy sits beside the value it copies, so confirming there is confirming where the user is looking

useInstead.when: copying is a page action that may collapse into an overflow menu — the Copy run ID in a record's header
useInstead.why: a confirmation drawn on the button cannot be seen once the button is in a menu; a Button that confirms with a Toast can be

composition.note: Beside the value, after it. Icon-only in a dense row, with `label` saying what is copied; with a visible label where there is room.
composition.example: {runId} showForManualCopy(text)} />

tertiary.use: the default — beside the value it copies

secondary.use: among other actions, as the only copy of something

sm.use: in tables, description lists and other dense rows

lg.use: beside a large value, such as a one-time key shown once

requires: `label` that says what is copied when `isIconOnly` — "Copy run ID", not "Copy"; it is the only name the button has
guarantees: a polite `status` region beside the button says `copiedLabel` on every press, a second press included, and `failedLabel` on a failure
the button's name follows what it shows: `label`, then `copiedLabel` for `resetAfter` milliseconds, then `label` again; another press restarts the time
the labels share one cell, so the button keeps its width and nothing beside it moves
icon-only, it is square, named by `label`, with `label` as its tooltip on hover and focus
without the Clipboard API — a non-secure origin — or when it is refused, it copies by selecting the text off-screen, and returns focus to the button
when both fail it shows and announces `failedLabel` with an alert icon and calls `onCopyError` with the text; it never claims a copy that did not happen
`value` as a function is read at the press, so it copies what is current
notes: on `onCopyError`, put the text where it can be selected by hand — a Toast holding it, or a read-only Input — so the user is never left without it
a secret shown once, like a new API key, should also be visible in full beside the button: a copy that failed must not be the only way to get it

antiPatterns.why: the hand-built one has no name, gives no confirmation, is silent to a screen reader, and fails without a word on a non-secure origin

antiPatterns.dont: a Toast that says "Copied" for a CopyButton
antiPatterns.why: it confirms in a corner the user is not looking at, and stacks up when they copy several things in a row

antiPatterns.dont: <CopyButton isIconOnly label="Copy" /> beside three different values
antiPatterns.do: label="Copy run ID", label="Copy agent ID", …
antiPatterns.why: three buttons named "Copy" cannot be told apart by name, and a screen reader's list of buttons reads "Copy, Copy, Copy"
